$comment: A fleet is ten jobs with ten models. `roleModels.<lane>.chain` is the ordered list of models that can serve that lane, best first, and the first rung the profile's `maxRetention` ceiling allows is the one that runs it. A chain is therefore ordered WITHIN this profile's ceiling, not globally: a ceiling of zero-retention puts the best zero-retention model for the job first, which is not always the best model for the job overall. The router walks the same chain when a route is spent. No model name in a lane is a promise that it will still exist next month, which is why every lane has a chain.
title: Ten jobs, zero-retention models only
notes: The default. Every lane resolves to a model whose provider states a zero-retention policy: no training, nothing kept. The cost is that six of the ten jobs run on a second-choice model - the planner loses beam (30-day retention) and the reviewer loses Nemotron 3 Ultra - so this is the floor, not the ceiling. The chains are ordered within the ceiling rather than copied from `fleet-all`: `locate` takes deepseek because it publishes a `low` effort level that longcat does not, and `vision` takes deepseek because it is the zero-retention route the provider kept for image reads. `fleet-all` gives every lane the model built for it.

utility.why: Cheapest route measured for a short auxiliary call: 49 reasoning tokens and 7.2s for a title, against 110 and 13.4s on big-pickle and 332 and 10.6s on nemotron-3.5-super-vl. It is also in every chain of this fleet, so a failover cannot leave the utility route pointing at a model that is not in the fleet.
